title: CAIQ snapshot proof and short-lived customer claim pilot
creator: Elena Park
description:
Problem: Enterprise buyers frequently request up-to-date CAIQ/SIG answers but internal legal + security teams prefer short, verifiable proofs rather than full document dumps. Generating bespoke attestations for every contract is expensive and slows sales.

Proposal: Pilot a CAIQ 'snapshot proof' artifact -- a compact cryptographic hash of a curated CAIQ answer set (per customer/contract) + metadata (timestamp, release tag, scope) signed by Redwood. Alongside the snapshot we will generate a short-lived customer claim token (signed, TTL 30 days) that references the snapshot hash and enumerates high-impact answers. This allows customers to present a lightweight, verifiable claim during procurement review and for Redwood to provide an on-demand, low-effort evidence path.

Scope: prototype backend signing service, CAIQ answer set selection UI in Console for solutions/legal to assemble a snapshot, token generation endpoint for sales to mint claims, and an experiment tying token issuance to a small pricing credit for evidence-heavy contracts.

Out of scope: full blockchain anchoring, enterprise-led key escrow, automated question-by-question proof generation (we will do snapshot-level hashes only).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Console UI to select CAIQ subset and create a named snapshot (name, scope, hash) exists.
2) Backend service signs snapshot metadata and stores snapshot record with immutable hash and timestamp.
3) Token generation API issues short-lived (configurable TTL) signed claim tokens referencing snapshot hash and listing 3-6 highlighted answers.
4) Basic verification endpoint verifies signature and TTL; internal docs created for Sales/SE usage.
5) Pilot experiment collects metrics and ties issuance to a configurable pricing credit rule.
6) Security review signoff received before pilot launch.

Eng: token minting endpoint with TTL and revocation flag

updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff meeting with Eng (Anna Ruiz, Marcus Chen), Security (Priya Nair), Legal (Samir Patel), Sales Ops (Jasmine Liu). Agreed MVP = snapshot hash + token referencing up to 6 answers.
2026-03-06: Security advised using customer-scoped signer keys via KMS; KMS integration estimated 2 days for PoC. Action: Eng to prototype with dev key and KMS shim.
2026-03-09: Design review — Console flow mockups reviewed. PM requested an inline explanation for customers describing "what the token proves". Design to iterate and return by 3/12.
2026-03-12: Decision: token TTL default 30 days, configurable by Solutions/Legal up to 90 days. Revocation will be a simple flag checked by verification endpoint (no push revocation for MVP).

2026-03-14: Pricing experiment scoped: for pilot customers, issuing a claim token will unlock a one-time $250 evidence credit applied to contract onboarding fees. Finance approved pilot budget with 10-customer cap.
2026-03-15: Security review checklist created (confluence/SPEC-981234); flagged requirement to record all tokens issued in audit log. Security to sign off before deploy to staging.
